description: The right plot in Figure 4 illustrates the relationship between Accuracy@1 (%) on geometry problems (Geomverse) and the number of child nodes (tree width) for rollout search, comparing two large vision-language models: GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. The x-axis, labeled “Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width),” is on a linear scale ranging from 1 to 7, with tick marks at integer values. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy@1 (%)”, is also linear, spanning from 15 to 35, with major gridlines every 5 units. The plot features two lines: GPT-4o is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers, and Claude-3.5-Sonnet by a solid light purple line with circular markers. For GPT-4o, Accuracy@1 starts at 24.4% at tree width 1, rises to 28.9% at width 3, peaks at 34.4% at width 5, then declines to 31.1% at width 7. For Claude-3.5-Sonnet, the accuracy begins at 26.7% at width 1, dips slightly to 27.8% at width 3, then steadily decreases to 24.4% at width 5 and further to 20.0% at width 7. The plot visually demonstrates an inverted U-shaped trend for GPT-4o and a generally declining trend for Claude-3.5-Sonnet as tree width increases.
